name: Proof Canvas
summary: One mathematical object built step by step and then transformed, with every variable keeping its colour for the whole film. For theorems, probability, geometry and quantitative arguments.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Restate the claim and say why it has to be true.
visual_job.hero: A single mathematical object (lattice, curve, construction) that is constructed, then transformed.

use_when: The film builds an argument, derivation or construction.
A surprising claim is resolved by a visible key move.
Quantities are abstract (probabilities, sequences, geometry), not measurements.
avoid_when: The numbers are real-world measurements over time (use data-ledger).
The subject is a software or physical system (use systems-blueprint).

alternates.when: Equation-led film with almost no diagram.
The brief asks for dark (polya-recurrence used it).

scene_grammar.formula: State the surprising claim as a contrast between two objects shown side by side.
Define the object by building it from nothing; name each variable once and give it a colour.
Build the argument one visible change at a time; a variable keeps its colour and position throughout.
The key move: highlight, transform or collapse the object so the reason is visible.
The claim restated over the final state of the object, with the numbers.
What changes in the next case (another dimension, another rule), shown on the same object.

motion.signature: Construction, not appearance: each element is drawn or derived from the previous one.
motion.continuous_layer: The constructed object keeps running (seeded walkers, slow rotation, scale drift) so a held argument is never a held frame.
avoid: Decorative motion unrelated to the argument.

rules.ending: Restate the claim over the final state of the constructed object.

anti_patterns.pattern: A scene tail with nothing left to build.
anti_patterns.why: Polya's closing scene had ~5.5 s of near-empty frame while narration continued; found only after the render. List every visual change time against audio/timeline.json before rendering, closing and quote scenes first.

anti_patterns.pattern: The important minority buried under the majority.
anti_patterns.why: In the 12-bird swarm the returned birds were hidden under escaped trails. Draw the important minority last and thicker, and check a snapshot before the full render.

anti_patterns.pattern: Narration over a frame that does not change for more than max_beat_gap_sec.
anti_patterns.why: Breaks the anti-laziness rule. motion-qa flagged 41 s of 70 (cloud), 44 s of 92 (fridge), 79 s of 98 (Korea) as static or low-energy. Plan one visual event per 2-3 s from measured onsets and give every scene a drift layer (Studio.space.drift).

anti_patterns.pattern: A headline that restates the narration.
anti_patterns.why: Fridge headlines repeated 82-83% of the voice, which wastes the strongest text slot. Use it for what the voice does not say (the number, the contrast, the date). A caption band is a legitimate repeat.

anti_patterns.pattern: Named or shown things the viewer cannot read an explanation of (anonymous chips, a badge with no field, a term with no definition).
anti_patterns.why: game-theory-trust closed on a ranked column of unlabelled chips and the words 'the simplest entry'; the owner's review called it a knowledge gap that leaves the viewer uncomfortable. Where narration cannot afford the explanation, the visuals carry it: definition card, legend, rule written out, source line. See motion-graphics-designer section G.

reference_projects.note: Only mathematics film so far; used dark-tech, 73 s portrait.

open_questions: No equation typesetting (KaTeX or similar) exists in the studio runtime; equations are set as ordinary text. Decide whether that is enough for derivations.

revisions.change: Initial version. Narration budget is the top of the deliberate (documentary) range, 27 words per 10 s, because the viewer needs time to think. Not yet calibrated against a film made to it: polya-recurrence (29-39 words per 10 s at am_adam 1.15) exceeds it in every scene.

Added the anti-pattern 'named or shown things the viewer cannot read an explanation of': the visuals carry the information the narration skips (motion-graphics-designer section G). No other rule changed.
